categories.main_business_segments: Quants Research Institute Holdings, Inc. operates three main business segments: M&A advisory (M&A仲介事業), consulting (コンサルティング事業), and other businesses including asset management consulting and operating lease services. The M&A advisory segment is the core, providing technology-driven M&A intermediation, while the consulting segment focuses on strategy, IT, and DX transformation for corporate clients. The 'other' segment covers asset management consulting and operating leases through subsidiaries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary AI algorithms, natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning to automate and optimize the matching of M&A buyers and sellers. It has developed in-house DX systems to streamline internal workflows, automate document generation, and monitor sales activities. The integration of generative AI for document drafting and NLP for extracting relevant buyer candidates from large datasets is central to its technology-driven approach.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are Japanese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) seeking business succession or strategic M&A, as well as larger corporations looking for acquisitions. The consulting segment serves a broad range of Japanese companies requiring strategic, IT, and digital transformation support. The end markets are predominantly domestic Japanese businesses, with some expansion into Southeast Asia via Singapore.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are primarily based in Japan, with headquarters in Tokyo and regional offices in Osaka and Nagoya. In 2024, it established a subsidiary in Singapore to pursue cross-border M&A opportunities in Southeast Asia. The vast majority of revenue and assets remain concentrated in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: Quants Research Institute Holdings operates downstream in the value chain, directly interfacing with end clients as an M&A intermediary and management consultant. It does not manufacture physical goods but provides professional services and technology-enabled solutions directly to business clients.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The strategic focus is on expanding the scale and efficiency of M&A intermediation through continued investment in AI and DX systems, shortening deal cycles, and reducing client costs. R&D is centered on enhancing AI matching algorithms, integrating generative AI and NLP, and automating the entire M&A process. The company also prioritizes talent acquisition and training, and is investing in the growth of its consulting segment.
categories.revenue_model: The primary revenue model is success-based fees from M&A transactions, with no upfront or interim fees for sellers, and a partial interim fee for buyers at the letter of intent or due diligence stage. Consulting revenues are generated through project-based or retainer contracts for strategic, IT, and DX advisory services. The operating lease and asset management segments generate additional, though minor, fee-based income.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other Japanese M&A intermediaries such as Nihon M&A Center and Strike, as well as large consulting firms. The company differentiates itself through its proprietary AI-driven matching system, fully success-based fee structure for sellers, and rapid deal execution. It is positioned as a technology leader and innovator in the Japanese M&A advisory market.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending September 2025, consolidated revenue was approximately 16.6 billion yen, with net profit attributable to shareholders of 2.75 billion yen. The company has experienced rapid growth in recent years, though FY2025 saw a slight revenue increase (+0.3%) and a significant profit decline due to upfront investments in consulting and talent. The workforce grew to 690 employees, reflecting ongoing expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company’s value proposition centers on faster, more accurate M&A matching through proprietary AI and DX, a fully success-based fee model for sellers (no upfront or interim fees), and a significantly shorter average deal cycle (7.2 months). Its technology reduces human error and levels the playing field for less experienced advisors, while its in-house systems and data-driven approach create high barriers to imitation.
